claims.statement: The procedure declares FPT/GHEC/GHES with plan/visibility limits in the product reusable and administrator/edit-repository-rules permission. This is an instruction source, not owner approval to change live estate settings.
Branch/tag rulesets control selected branches/tags; the source also mentions repository and tag rename restrictions without supplying a separate observed repository-rename enforcement mechanism.
Push rulesets restrict paths, lengths, extensions and sizes across eligible private/internal fork networks; bypass roles, teams and apps must be reviewed with that inherited scope.
The guide also links organization rulesets for Team/Enterprise organizations; repository instructions do not establish estate-wide adoption.
JSON ruleset import and external ruleset-recipes are available under repo-rules-management (FPT/GHEC/GHES>=3.19). External recipes were not treated as reviewed source text.
Branch/tag targeting uses File.fnmatch, where * does not match slash, qa/* matches one directory depth, and qa/**/* includes recursive matching.

The fnmatch-options reusable excludes backslash quoting, complemented sets and EXTGLOB but literally attributes those limits to branch protection. Its inclusion in a ruleset guide does not prove parity of all rule engines.

Metadata regex rules require selecting a regex operator; otherwise patterns are literal. The reusable identifies RE2 and multiline (?m) for multiple-line messages, with signed-off trailers requiring deliberate compatibility checks.

The regex reusable claims positive lookahead can substitute for unsupported negative lookahead; the linked primary RE2 syntax lists BOTH (?=re) and (?!re) unsupported. The workaround is not a safe recommended pattern.

The Windows branch-name example uses an anchored single-character class without repetition yet claims it matches my-branch. That literal pattern cannot match the multi-character example; retain the defect instead of adopting it.
The reusable’s SemVer, 50-character message and Fixes/conventional-commit regexes are illustrative source examples, not mandatory local version or commit policy.
Active enforces, Disabled does not enforce, and feature-gated Evaluate observes without blocking. The source recommends Evaluate for testing, which is not an activation receipt.

Creating a branch/tag ruleset uses repository Settings and the pinned Rulesets sidebar then Rulesets route, new branch/tag ruleset and name with optional enforcement-status change. Default enforcement is Disabled; a saved ruleset can remain non-enforcing.

Bypass may admit administrators, eligible organization roles, custom writer roles, non-secret teams and apps/Dependabot, with extra enterprise/Copilot or deploy-key actors gated by product. Delegated bypass approval is separate from ordinary write permission.
For branch/tag rulesets, pull-request-only bypass preserves a PR audit trail; Always bypass also permits direct pushes. Neither proves that the bypassed changes satisfy every ordinary requirement.
Select include/exclude branch/tag target criteria using fnmatch or explicit names. Multiple criteria require applicability review before combining rules.
Selected checks must be entered and added by name; strict/up-to-date protection requires at least one actual defined status check. Selecting strict alone does not establish any check requirement.

Metadata restrictions support consistency, not a substitute for security checks; patterns are literal unless regex is selected, descriptions are visible, and Evaluate can reveal mismatches. The included metadata note repeats the all-commits squash requirement that conflicts with the available-rules resulting-commit-only statement.
Create saves the ruleset; immediate enforcement depends on Active status. Feature-gated insights in Evaluate show would-be failures without demonstrating blocked pushes.

Push ruleset creation uses the eligible repository’s Settings, pinned Rulesets sidebar then Rulesets, and new-push-ruleset route; it applies across the fork network rather than branch/tag target criteria.
Name the push ruleset and optionally change enforcement status from the included default Disabled; leaving it unchanged creates no active enforcement.
Only actors with root-repository bypass grants can bypass fork push rulesets; the guide repeats the eligible-role choices and conditional product actors.

Configure desired push restrictions with full or partial paths and optional path/size exceptions where gated; path length, extension and size constraints are different controls, not interchangeable filters.
Create and available insights complete the push procedure; reading these steps does not certify active enforcement, rejected-push behavior, effective bypass, rollback or estate rollout.

scope: Primary reading of full pinned article and recursively included dependencies. Reviewed source statements only; no adoption or live platform verification.
